subject: Toward 1.0: rival personalities, deeper combat, practice duels and release evidence (#41)
body:
* Stop the compact-battle board height failing on sub-pixel layout

The assertion wanted each .battle-board at least 40px tall and CI measured
39.649, so the run failed on a difference no player can see. It has now
failed three times on unrelated changes: Dependabot #12 (workflow YAML only)
and #14, and the main run after #25.

Rounds the measured height before comparing, which keeps the usable-strip
intent while tolerating sub-pixel layout. A genuine collapse still fails.

Also refreshes the committed development change feed from merged main history.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add the rival guestbook, duel key moments and four practice lessons

Record wins, losses, draws and concessions per guest with the latest
reward, learned recipe and up to five public exchanges. Teach resource
payment, counterspell responses, blocking and targeted protection with
replayable borrowed-card lessons that use the real battle commands and
never change ownership or rewards. Browser runs now write screenshots
to Playwright's per-test output; `npm run test:screenshots` refreshes
docs/screenshots on request (DH-016).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Give rivals six tactical personalities and deepen combat rules

Every guest now pilots their recipe with an aggressive, defensive,
reactive, recursive, evasive or Hero-minded personality that changes
casting priority, removal timing, held response mana, protection,
counter thresholds, attack risk, blocks, gang blocks, Hero abilities
and attack destinations from the public table only. Combat gains
per-attacker destinations, any number of blockers per attacker with
attacker-ordered damage, Overrun spill through every blocker and
toggled block assignment; older saves load single blockers as lists.
The guest who lost the last meeting opens the next duel.

Add scripts/performance.ts (browser-emulated delivery report), widen
scripts/balance.ts to a 1,680-duel matrix from both seats with the
in-game autoplay in the keeper's seat, propose the 1.0 scope in
docs/RELEASE_SCOPE.md, run the browser suite under Playwright's
Firefox with PW_BROWSER=firefox, and assert that phone panel headings
never meet the close button (DH-017).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Let guests speak in the guestbook and check a delivery budget

Each of the twenty guests carries four original rivalry lines chosen
by the saved record, and the guestbook names their tactical
personality with counterplay guidance for the keeper. The duel
welcome keeps the opening-seat note. scripts/performance.ts gains a
proposed delivery budget and a --check mode that fails on breaches;
the production build currently meets it. Browser tests skip
Chromium-only automation and WebGL scenes under Firefox instead of
failing, tolerate sub-pixel 44px controls and fall back when Firefox
rejects image decode().

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add borrowed-recipe practice duels and style-aware autoplay

The card table offers a free practice duel: borrow any of the 28
recipes against any guest with no reward, record, recipe unlock or
clock; older saves default the new battle flag to false. Autoplay now
pilots the keeper's recipe in the style its own cards suggest, the
performance report pages through the whole binder, and
docs/RELEASE_ACCEPTANCE.md gathers dated evidence per scope area. The
balance matrix rerun shows the recipe spread survives the pilot
change, naming recall density versus Quickstep pressure as the first
tuning target.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Block with one scored planner on both seats

Extract the rival block planner as planBlocks over the public table
and let the keeper's autoplay use it, in the style the keeper's own
recipe suggests, instead of chump-blocking every attacker. Measure the
matrix again (keeper 46%, recursion recipes 73% and about 80% as
rivals, fast Ember 13–27%), record a reverted body-shape experiment
and a recipe-level tuning proposal for the owner, and let the balance
script run subsets with BALANCE_RECIPES, BALANCE_SEEDS and BALANCE_OUT.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix destinations, the second-seat redraw and lethal aim after review

An attacker explicitly sent at the hearth is no longer redirected to
the default Hero; the free redraw stays available on the keeper's
first turn after a guest opens, redrawing the whole hand; a rival that
sees lethal aims every attacker at the hearth. Cache cast scores in
the AI's main phase, reuse the game's shuffle in the balance script,
write the performance report once and release its preview server on
failure.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Poll for loaded paintings in the folio browser scenario

Firefox rejects decode() for some paintings and reports them complete a
frame later, so the one-shot check flaked; poll until every hand card's
painting is complete at its native size.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Publish Pages from a locally verified gh-pages build

Add scripts/deploy-pages.sh (npm run deploy:pages), which copies a
production build made for the Pages base path into the gh-pages branch
after the local checks, so publishing spends no Actions minutes. The
Publish game workflow stays available by manual dispatch only.

* Balance pass 1: rebuild the fast Ember recipes and trim recursion

Cinder March Vanguard, The Kiln Wakes and Root & Cinder move their
curve to cost two through five, prefer Overrun and Skyborne bodies,
favor Spellcraft and Gather companions and carry four burn spells and
three pumps. The Returning Grove, The Thornbound Path, Reedwater Revel
and Debts of the Long Ash each lose one recall and one removal copy.
No card definition, ID, painting, authored recipe or save changes; the
exact-recipe fixtures are regenerated deliberately for the seven
recipes. Autoplay's deck style counts burn and pump together and
recognises the trimmed recursion lists. Measured before and after with
the subset runs and the full 1,680-duel matrix; the recursion
archetype remains the next target.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Wait for the Pages build when publishing and record the second publish

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Check the change ledger against its own head commit

The pull-request Checks run tests GitHub's merge ref, whose first parent is
main, so the branch snapshot's newest commit was missing from the
first-parent walk and the ledger test failed with index -1. The test now
requires the snapshot's head to be an ancestor of HEAD on any parent line
and compares the snapshot with the first-parent history as of that commit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Balance pass 2: separate the recursion recipes and sharpen The Kiln Wakes

The Returning Grove prefers Mourning companions alone; The Thornbound Path,
which had resolved to the same sixty cards, now favors Skyborne, Reach and
Venom bodies with two recalls and a shield; The Kiln Wakes trades a pump and
two mana rocks for a fifth burn, a removal and a draw. Measured against a
fixed six-recipe panel from both seats (BALANCE_OPPONENTS, new) and the full
1,680-duel matrix: The Returning Grove 73% → 45% for the keeper and 77% → 70%
as a rival, The Thornbound Path 73% → 53% and 67% → 57%, The Kiln Wakes
28% → 38% and 47% → 50%. Recipe digests regenerated for the three recipes; a
test keeps all 28 recipes distinct; the spell packages are a lookup table.
The asset-hash test gets a 60 s budget.

* Record the gh-pages publication of 7cfbaa1

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add the synthesized tavern soundscape with separate layer volumes

src/ui/soundscape.ts derives table cues from the public battle events and
table changes after each command (payment, arrival, cast, response,
countered, resolve, combat, hurt, heal, fallen, turn, won, lost, drawn) and
runs two ambient layers: a hearth of low filtered noise with random crackles
and a room of slow murmur with an occasional cup set down. Cards, Hearth and
Room volumes are independent; the controls sit in the tavern menu and in
Table options, share one soundscape and persist as a device preference,
never in the save. Nothing in the simulation changed. Unit tests cover the
cue derivation and the preference round trip; a Chromium scenario enables
sounds, plays a turn and reloads. The resource-art scenario now waits for
the painting to decode instead of sampling once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add a thirty-day scripted shop-loop diagnostic

scripts/economy.ts runs four keeper policies through the public commands at
the interface's pace and writes docs/reports/economy.json: a steady keeper at
the default price nets about 161 crowns a day from 10 sales among 18
visitors, dips below the starting purse only on day one, and holds about
5,700 crowns by day thirty; 40-crown and 56-crown pricing net less; a growing
keeper with the dining wing and welcome skills nets 318. Storage is the
binding limit and no path leads to debt. Recorded as scripted evidence for
the shop-loop acceptance; human playtests remain open. The development README
gains a Diagnostics section for the three report scripts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Pin the balance roadmap evidence to the working tree

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep a save fixture per published build

src/sim/fixtures/published-d44a11e-save.json is captured from the published
build's simulation after a day of trade, a delivery, an opened pack, a
learned skill, a prepared recipe and a duel in progress.
src/sim/published-saves.test.ts loads every published fixture unchanged,
round-trips it through the local ledger and plays a bell and a duel step
from it, so a later schema change must migrate these deliberately.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Re-measure delivery after the soundscape and tidy the roadmap evidence

The performance script now defaults its base path to the one the build in
dist was made for, so a Pages build measures without PAGES_BASE. The report
re-run on this build stays within budget (1.08 MiB first play, 2.4 s on
fast 3G, 8.7 s on slow 3G, 60 fps across the 60 s duel). A duplicate
evidence path in the rival-stories roadmap item produced a React key
warning on the helper page; evidence lists are deduplicated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Fix the review findings: structured battle events and a tidier soundscape

Battle events carry structured fields (payment, cast, response, resolve
with card ID and owner) so sound cues switch on kinds instead of log
wording; older saves keep text-derived kinds. A fresh duel at the same
table resets the cue snapshot, the soundscape starts after a reload with
sounds on, suspends when sounds are turned off and skips bursts while
suspended. The economy script reads costs from content, the performance
script falls back to / for a relative base, and the balance script rejects
unknown recipe ids and non-integer samples.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add a host keeper to the shop-loop diagnostic

The host opens the kitchen and bar and cooks by a fixed rule: about 17
servings a day and level 20 by day thirty, but 5.7 pack sales a day instead
of 22 because two thirds of arrivals then come to eat or drink. Recorded in
the readiness, status and acceptance docs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Default local Playwright runs to two workers and document the lean local loop

This 32-core workstation gave Playwright sixteen workers by default, which
crowded out other sessions' processes. Local runs now use two workers
(PW_WORKERS overrides) with no retries, and the development README states
the lean procedure: unit suite plus the specs that cover a change, the whole
Chromium suite once before publishing, Firefox one file at a time.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Trim the testing method: tiers, smoke tag, review-only screenshots and cases

docs/development/TESTING.md states what runs when: `npm run check` and
the covering spec files while developing, `npm run test:smoke` (six
@smoke Chromium scenarios, ~30 s) before a commit, the ordinary
`npm run test:gameplay` once before a publish, and the review run,
`npm run test:firefox` (one file at a time) and diagnostics only at an
agreed checkpoint. Ordinary runs take no documentation screenshots
(`docScreenshot` is a no-op outside UPDATE_DOC_SCREENSHOTS=1) and run
one representative of each equivalent case through `reviewCases`, so
the suite is 55 scenarios in 2.1 min at two workers; the review run
keeps all 64. CI runs the checks tier and the Pages build only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Sweep the whole catalogue through the TypeSafe gate (#25)
body:
Scopes the questions so they can judge every set honestly, then records a
judgment for all 1,040 cards.

The boundary questions (Ashfall cause, Failing cause, disputed questions
settled as fact, graphic harm) apply catalogue-wide. A stone answering again
only applies from The Long Ash onward, because before RR 2311 that is canon.
Paintability, mechanic fit, framing and name confusability apply to authored
sets only: the older sets repeat one set tagline as every card's flavor, keep
their scenes in the briefs, and are named procedurally with deliberate
instant/sorcery twins, so judging them there reported the design, not defects.

Adds a catalogue-wide question for Theandril's open questions being settled as
fact, and a test asserting no judged card carries a blocking flag.

No blocking flags across 1,040 cards.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

body:
Groups the open Dependabot updates into one change: react and @types/react
19.3, three 0.186.0, zod 4.6.2, lucide-react 1.44.0, the development group
(@playwright/test 1.63, @types/node 26.5.1, vite 8.3), pnpm/action-setup

subject: Add The Quiet, a thirteenth 80-card volume (#19)
body:
* Add The Quiet, a thirteenth 80-card volume

Release 13 covers RR 2311–2313 from Book chapter VII: the stones fall
silent and every bargain becomes local. 80 Ember/Grove cards in three
strands (The Quiet Stones, The Near Fields, Beacon and Rider) use only
existing engine effects. Two ordinary-card recipes bridge to Rekindled
Hearths and The Long Ash, and older saves gain an empty Quiet shelf.

Card text passes a cached TypeSafe (jev-1.13.0) gate for lore boundaries,
paintability, framing and name confusion before any art is commissioned.
Each painting is one Codex built-in generation from its exact brief,
processed by the vendored factory and approved by exact hash after visual
review; five first generations were rejected and replaced. A review guard
checks that written findings report no defect before approval.

The helper page now reads catalog counts from a build-generated summary,
and structural tests use live set and card counts. Released baselines
stay pinned.
